title: The Gas In Your Party Balloon Is Running Out
note: Fourth 3D short, written for 3D from the queued helium-supply-squeeze story. One number at most per beat; the closing says why you care and asks. Every claim is in 'sources' with the source's own wording.
lines: The gas in party balloons is running out, and we can't make more.
Almost all of it comes up from natural gas wells, made underground as radioactive rock slowly breaks down.
And once it's out, it floats up through the air and escapes into space. It's gone for good.
Its biggest job isn't balloons. About a quarter of it keeps hospital MRI machines cold enough to work.
So every balloon we let go is helium a hospital might need. Would you still buy one?

sources.claim: It is running out and cannot be made again
sources.says: Terrestrial helium is a non-renewable resource because once released into the atmosphere, it promptly escapes into space. Its supply is thought to be rapidly diminishing.

sources.claim: It comes from natural gas wells, made by radioactive decay underground
sources.says: Most terrestrial helium present today is created by the natural radioactive decay of heavy radioactive elements ... This radiogenic helium is trapped with natural gas in concentrations as great as 7% by volume
once released into the atmosphere, it promptly escapes into space

sources.claim: Its biggest use, about a quarter, cools MRI magnets
sources.says: its largest single use, consuming about a quarter of production ... most of which involves cooling the superconducting magnets in medical MRI scanners and NMR spectrometers
While balloons are perhaps the best-known use of helium, they are a minor part of all helium use.

sets_why: the party aisle where you buy it, the gas well where it comes from, the open sky by the water where it leaves, the hospital bay where it works, back to the aisle
ideas: his big bunch of balloons shrivels and sags in his hand
he cranks a wellhead's valve wheel and gas from the ground swells a balloon on the pipe
he jumps for an escaping balloon and it gets away into the sky
he pours a smoking flask of freezing helium into a giant scanner
he ties the last balloon down instead of letting it go
storyboard: 1 hook (store): close, waist up in the party aisle, Data holds ONE huge shiny red balloon by its string right beside his face; it goes limp, sags in on itself and drops down its string to hang off his fist like a wet sock; his face falls and he looks at us, alarmed.

2 well (gas_field): a big red wellhead pipe stands out of the bare ground right beside Data, a limp empty balloon flopped over its open top; a big yellow valve wheel stands up on it facing us, right in front of him, and he cranks it round and round by its red handle; the balloon on the pipe rises and swells huge and round with the gas coming up out of the ground; he looks at us, pleased.

3 escape (dock): low on the dock with open sky behind, Data lets go of a big balloon by mistake; it rises past his face, he jumps with both arms up and misses the string by a hand, and it climbs away into the sky, shrinking to a dot; he lands and stares after it.

4 MRI (hospital): close beside a giant MRI scanner ring, Data holds FOUR balloons by their strings; he winds ONE of the four strings round a steel cleat on the scanner and draws back his fist with the other three; the tied balloon bobs at the scanner, frost creeps white over the ring and its lamp switches from red to green; he holds up his three and looks at us: about a quarter of our helium keeps hospital scanners cold.

5 payoff (store): close in the party aisle, Data holds one pink balloon by its string, looks up at it, then turns to us and holds it out TOWARD THE LENS, offering it, eyebrows up, a questioning face held for about a second to the end while the balloon bobs: would you still buy one?
